quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your driving lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.
You signal your intention for three seconds.
You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough space before returning to your lane. Check your inside rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Driving faster than traffic increases your collision risk. Driving slower than traffic also increases risk because it can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles on your left and parked vehicles on your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Down the middle, between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle, between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle. Balance your position between both sides.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the road will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.
Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with vehicles arriving at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Other vehicles proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Only check the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Only check the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check that the lane is clear. Always look behind and to the side of your vehicle before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers may not see you directly behind them. Increase your following distance so you can see around the sides and see the road ahead.

questions.question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Yield your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent collisions.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to drive on if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can also affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs affect driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can also affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, hay fever, and anxiety. The law says you cannot drive if any drug impairs your ability to drive safely. It does not matter if the drug is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: When you approach a curve, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Keep your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you approach a curve or turn, slow down. You can speed up again after you pass the middle of the turn.

questions.question: On a freeway, look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Watch for traffic changes ahead on the freeway. Look for signals from other drivers. Watch for vehicles entering at on-ramps. Be ready for quick changes in road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, you should:

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly get back on the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly get back on the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately if your wheels drop off the edge. Instead, slow down. Check for traffic. Then slowly turn back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: All work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. To prevent it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down in rainy weather to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast can cause your tires to ride up on the water. This makes them lose contact with the road, and your vehicle becomes hard to control.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear to slow down.
Release the gas pedal slowly.
Pump the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal slowly.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal slowly if your tires lose contact with the road. Do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before you try to stop or turn.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for something. This sign warns you that pedestrians may be crossing.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. You cannot turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You must use low beams whenever you are:

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start your turn from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street, always start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: When is it okay to drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes going your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when bad weather makes it hard to see?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther back from the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you cannot see.

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Wait until you can drive completely through the intersection.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can drive completely through the intersection.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter the intersection if you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass. A solid yellow line means traffic on that side cannot pass.

questions.question: Who must a left-turning driver yield to?

options.text: Cars passing you.
Cars coming toward you.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must let oncoming traffic pass first. Turn only when it is safe and oncoming traffic is not affected.

questions.question: What is a result of driving too fast?

options.text: It does not increase crash risk.
It improves your ability to react to danger.
It often leads to risky driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often leads to risky driving decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky driving decisions.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange warning signs.

questions.question: What does this pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn allowed on red.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no passing zone begins.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. No one can pass from either direction.
